summary: Sanders County, MT: a 1909 pole tower on Taft Summit burned in the 1910 fire and fell into power lines; an L-4 tower followed; a crow's nest is reported still there.

facts.design: 35-foot pole platform tower built 1909; an L-4 tower built in the 1930s (firelookout.com)
facts.status_note: L-4 tower destroyed in the 1950s; firelookout.com says a crow's nest half a mile east is still there (undated); montanalookouts marks the site Removed

events.note: Two of the tower's legs burned in the Great Idaho Fire; the tower fell into adjacent Montana Power Company lines

evidence.supports: location: 7 miles ENE of Lookout Pass, Sanders County
the site is on the Lolo National Forest
first tower: 35-foot pole platform tower built in 1909
evidence.quote: A 35' pole platform tower was constructed in 1909

evidence.supports: two legs burned in the 1910 fire; tower fell into Montana Power Company lines
evidence.quote: only to have two of its legs burned in the Great Idaho Fire of 1910, causing it to fall into adjacent Montana Power Company lines.

evidence.supports: the 1910 fire burned about three million acres across northern Idaho and western Montana
the 1910 fire was in Northern Idaho and Western Montana
evidence.quote: in Northern Idaho and Western Montana

evidence.supports: L-4 tower built in the 1930s and destroyed in the 1950s
evidence.quote: In the 1930's, an L-4 tower was built, but destroyed in the 1950's.

evidence.supports: crow's nest half a mile east, reported still there (undated)
evidence.quote: There was also a crow's nest 1/2 mile east, which is still there.

evidence.supports: montanalookouts marks the site as removed, without a date
montanalookouts places the site on the Lolo National Forest
Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower as gone

notes_for_editor: The firelookout.com header R.I.P. 1909-1910 describes the first tower; the 1930s L-4 tower follows on the same page. No height is given for the L-4, so height_m is omitted. The 1930s and 1950s dates are decade-only, so they appear in the story text and design field, not as dated events. No staffing, fire-watch or access source was found. The 1910 fire context comes from Wikipedia, not a lookout source. The crow's nest remark is undated. The story does not describe the summit today.
